page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture (Neoverse-V1) running at 2.6 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes 3800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark testing, the r7gd.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. Its multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench ranks in the top 25%, supported by a strong PassMark CPU physics score. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier, and uncached read and write memory bandwidths both placing in the top 25%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top 25%, alongside strong static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier, and text generation for small LLM models is relatively poor, placing in the bottom 10%.

Given its ARM-based Graviton architecture and high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the r7gd.16xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency by delivering high resource density and memory bandwidth without the overhead of traditional x86 licensing. The inclusion of 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes it highly suitable for workloads requiring fast local scratch space. This instance is optimized for memory-intensive and storage-heavy applications, including high-performance databases, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
